title: The World's Religions: Our Great Wisdom Traditions
author: Huston Smith
publication_date: 1958 (originally published as 'The Religions of Man'), revised edition 1991
target_audience: General readers seeking an introduction to world religions
core_themes: Core beliefs and practices of the world's major religious traditions
Comparative understanding and respect for diverse wisdom traditions
The pursuit of meaning and transcendence
Interconnectedness of religious principles and human experience
The role and evolution of religion in human societies
primary_purpose: To introduce readers to the major world religions by exploring their fundamental teachings, practices, historical development, and cultural significance, fostering understanding, empathy, and appreciation for spiritual diversity.

structure_format.narrative_style: Accessible, respectful, and descriptive; avoids doctrinal debate or overt critique
structure_format.organization: Divided into chapters by major religion (Hinduism, Buddhism, Confucianism, Taoism, Islam, Judaism, Christianity, and a final chapter on Indigenous traditions), each examining beliefs, rituals, histories, and distinctive features

key_concepts_lessons: Each religion offers a unique perspective on the ultimate questions of life, death, meaning, and morality.
Religions shape the moral and ethical frameworks of societies.
Traditions adapt and evolve within cultural and historical contexts.
Understanding religions requires not just intellectual analysis, but an empathetic and experiential approach.
Despite surface differences, many religions share core concerns such as compassion, justice, and the quest for transcendence.
notable_features: Frequently used as a college introductory text
Highlights commonalities and differences without proselytizing
Focuses on lived experience as much as doctrine
cultural_historical_context: Written during a period of increasing globalization and interfaith engagement, the book emerged against a background of mid-20th-century curiosity about other cultures and belief systems. It has remained influential in a world seeking greater religious literacy and mutual respect.
reception_impact: One of the most widely read and respected introductions to comparative religion
Praised for its clarity, empathy, and comprehensive scope
Influential in public interfaith and multicultural education
Occasional criticism from specialists for lack of depth on some traditions
comparable_titles: A History of God by Karen Armstrong
Religions of the World by Lewis M. Hopfe
God Is Not One by Stephen Prothero
The Illustrated World's Religions by Huston Smith
